sourceNotes: Issue #263: first MPFB2 humanoid promoted into a station cast (OB triage patient Aisha Khan).

Issue #222: MPFB rail paints the proven bounds-derived scalp hair region (Anny automate_blender apply_mesh_native_scalp_hair_material_region) instead of the hand-authored UV sphere; no separate hair mesh remains. Textures remain out of scope by peer decision.

Issue #317: face targets now load through the proven TargetService path (body_param_stage.load_mpfb_face_shape_keys) instead of the MPFB UI operator, which read panel state and shipped zero face morphs. The #222 scalp-region Z-flip was also corrected: create_human faces -Y (measured), so the flip pushed the face to +Y, the face-band exclusion never fired, and the scalp paint covered the eyes/brows.

Issue #318: the candidate materializer strips MakeHuman's clothes and hair FITTING SHELLS with the MPFB-shipped ExportService.bake_modifiers_remove_helpers (remove_helpers=True), called after the face-target load so morph keys stay indexed to the full base topology. The shipped GLB drops from 36,972 to 26,756 tris (13,380 verts in Blender, MADR 0052 documented pair); the 32 FACS targets and 137-joint rig survive. The post-strip figure is an unclothed body; OB triage wardrobe staging is MADR 0052 P3.

Issue #321: the candidate materializer fits the CC0 toigo_basic_tucked_t-shirt onto the stripped basemesh via the PROVEN ClothesService.fit_clothes_to_human path (body_param_stage.py uses the same service for the hm08 library rail). The fit runs after the strip because .mhclo vertex refs index the 13,380-vert hm08 topology; the polo (helper-vert refs) is refused rather than fitted against absent indices. Garment material mat_makeclothes_library_toigo_t_shirt; garment 2,700 tris / 5,400 exported verts, skinned to the standard rig. Total 29,456 tris; 13 usable mouth targets and 137 joints unchanged. Garment choice is the least-wrong OB triage option: a hospital gown is not in the cached library and a scrub shirt is staff wear.
Not a realism gate pass; orchestrator grades the render and decides whether the material-class mismatch blocks adoption.
